cefrAlignment: Matches B1 (CEFR CV reading for information and argument: can recognise significant points and the line of argument in straightforward newspaper articles, and tell the writer's view from reported views): 205–240-word opinion column and advert/review texts with clear opinion signals.
examFidelity: The Yes/No/Not Given items are rigorous: each No contradicts a stated view of the writer, and each Not Given is truly absent. The variant is set correctly ('ynng'). The advert and review pair is a fair TOEIC Part 7 double passage, and the tips agree with exams.ts.
openConcerns: The fact/opinion/claim categories are simplified for B1. For example, 'Experts say this is the healthiest diet' is keyed as a claim, although it also contains an evaluative word. This is consistent with the lesson's own table, but a teacher may want to discuss it.
The TOEFL tag (Read an Academic Passage) fits the newspaper texts only loosely.
learnerOutcome: A learner can separate checkable facts, opinions and unsupported claims, tell the writer's view from quoted views, and answer simple Yes/No/Not Given questions.
